title: MGNN: Graph Neural Networks Inspired by Distance Geometry Problem

problem.claim: The paper concerns the expressive power and universality of graph neural networks, especially spatial GNNs.

gap.claim: Existing work lacks a comprehensive analysis of the universality of spatial GNNs from geometric and physical perspectives.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNNs are a prominent topic in machine learning.
GNNs are commonly categorized as spectral or spatial models.
Spectral GNN universality has been approached through improved basis-function design.
Spatial GNN expressivity has been studied through graph isomorphism tests and links to geometry and physics.
A comprehensive geometry- and physics-based analysis of spatial GNN universality remains missing.

unknowns: The proposed MGNN method or theoretical framework is not described.
No formal results, experiments, datasets, baselines, or numerical findings are supplied.
The abstract does not specify how distance geometry is used.
